# Jubilees Chapter 23 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 23:4 — describing the post-Flood lifespan decline

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "to grow old quickly, and to be full of their days on account of the manifold tribulations" | Literal, preserves "manifold tribulations" |
| LOGOS | "growing old quickly and reaching the fullness of their days — on account of the manifold tribulations" | Formal, same key phrase |
| PNEUMA | "aging faster, dying sooner. The cause was clear: the endless troubles that came from living wicked lives" | Dynamic, loses "manifold tribulations" as a term |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. "Manifold tribulations" is the established scholarly rendering of the Ge'ez phrase; it should be preserved as it reflects Jubilees' specific causal theology. PNEUMA's "endless troubles" is too casual for this formal eschatological diagnosis.

---

## 23:8 — lifespan reduction sequence

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "from one hundred years to seventy years, and from seventy years to fifty years..." | Full literal sequence with "years" repeated |
| LOGOS | "from one hundred years to seventy, from seventy to fifty..." | Same data, reduced repetition |
| PNEUMA | "from a hundred years to seventy, seventy to fifty..." | Further compressed |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. The sequence preserves all data points while avoiding excessive repetition of "years." EMET's full repetition is maximally literal but burdensome. PNEUMA drops the "from/to" structure that clarifies each step as a discrete decline.

---

## 23:17 — "no Satan" vs. "no adversary"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "there will be no Satan nor any evil destroyer" | Preserves "Satan" as proper name |
| LOGOS | "there will be no adversary and no evil destroyer" | Translates śāṭān as "adversary" |
| PNEUMA | "No adversary, no destroyer" | Compressed, "adversary" |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. In Jubilees, Mastema/Beliar is the named adversary; "Satan" here is functioning more as a title/noun (adversary) than the proper name it becomes in later tradition. "Adversary" preserves the meaning without importing the later theological weight of "Satan" as a proper name. EMET's rendering is defensible but potentially misleading.

---

## 23:19 — "their bones shall rest in the earth"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "their bones shall rest in the earth, and their spirits shall have much joy" | Literal, "much joy" |
| LOGOS | "their bones will rest in the earth, and their spirits will have great joy" | Formal, "great joy" |
| PNEUMA | "Their bones will rest in the earth, but their spirits will be overjoyed" | "overjoyed" — slight intensification |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. "Great joy" for the Ge'ez phrase is standard; PNEUMA's "overjoyed" is slightly stronger than the text warrants. The body/spirit distinction in this verse is theologically significant — Jubilees affirms bodily rest and spiritual joy as complementary, not opposed.

---

## 23:20 — "new creation" scope

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "until the day of the new creation when the heaven and earth and all their creatures shall be renewed like the powers of heaven" | Full literal |
| LOGOS | "until the day of the new creation — when heaven and earth and all their creatures shall be renewed, like the powers of the heavens" | Same, cleaner punctuation |
| PNEUMA | "until the day of the new creation, when heaven and earth and everything in them are made new, as fresh as the powers of heaven" | Dynamic, "as fresh as" for "like" |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. V.20 is a climactic verse and requires precision. "Like the powers of the heavens" should be retained as the simile is deliberate and theologically significant. PNEUMA's "as fresh as" is vivid but weakens the comparison's theological force.

---

**Total disagreements: 5**
